- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) or shows sharp negative swings, model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast growth to 3–5% above prior peak for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to recognize — reduce forecast slope slightly to reflect reversion bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price peaks — add 2–4% buffer to forecast when sentiment is positive and history shows upward momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model often misreads trend — use sentiment average over last 5 days to smooth forecast direction.
